about.title: Focused, attentive care for diabetes and everyday health
body: AVP Clinic was started with a simple goal — to give patients in Porur a place where diabetes and other chronic conditions are managed with real continuity of care, not rushed, one-off consultations.

Led by Dr. Priyadharshini V, Consultant Physician and Diabetologist, the clinic focuses on internal medicine and long-term diabetes management, with evening hours designed around working professionals and families.

Every visit includes time to actually discuss your reports, adjust your plan, and answer questions — because managing a chronic condition well depends on that ongoing relationship, not a single prescription.
highlights: Evening consultation hours for working professionals
General internal medicine under one roof

doctors.name: Dr. Priyadharshini V
doctors.qualification: MBBS, MD (General Medicine), Fellowship in Diabetology
doctors.bio: Dr. Priyadharshini V is a Consultant Physician and Diabetologist practicing at AVP Clinic, Porur. Her practice centers on diabetes management and general internal medicine, with an emphasis on building long-term treatment relationships rather than one-time consultations. She works closely with patients to manage blood sugar, blood pressure, and thyroid conditions through personalized, sustainable plans.

services.name: Diabetes Management & Monitoring
services.tagline: Personalized, ongoing care to keep your blood sugar in range
services.overview: Our diabetes management program focuses on continuous monitoring and plan adjustment — not a one-time prescription. Dr. Priyadharshini works with you to build a sustainable plan covering medication, diet, and lifestyle.

Ongoing plan adjustments based on trends

Plans built around your reports, not templates

faqs.question: How often should I get my diabetes monitored?
faqs.answer: This depends on how well-controlled your sugar levels are — typically every 4–12 weeks. Dr. Priyadharshini will set a schedule based on your HbA1c and overall trend.

faqs.question: Do I need to fast before my visit?
faqs.answer: If blood tests are planned, we'll let you know in advance whether fasting is required.

faqs.question: Do you accept walk-in patients?
faqs.answer: Yes, walk-ins are welcome, though we recommend booking an appointment in advance to minimize your wait time, especially during evening hours.

faqs.question: What should I bring for my first visit?
faqs.answer: Please bring any previous medical records, current medications or prescriptions, and recent lab reports if you have them. If you're managing diabetes, your recent blood sugar readings are helpful too.

faqs.question: How often should diabetes be monitored?
faqs.answer: This varies by patient, but most people on a stable plan are reviewed every 4–12 weeks, with more frequent monitoring if levels are still being brought under control.

faqs.answer: You can book directly through our appointment page on this site, or call the clinic to schedule a slot that works for you.

blogPosts.title: 5 Early Warning Signs of Type 2 Diabetes You Shouldn't Ignore
blogPosts.excerpt: Type 2 diabetes often develops quietly. Here are five early signs worth getting checked, before it progresses further.
blogPosts.author: Dr. Priyadharshini V
content: Type 2 diabetes rarely announces itself with a single dramatic symptom — it tends to show up as a handful of small, easy-to-dismiss changes that build up over months.
Frequent thirst and urination are among the earliest signs, caused by excess sugar pulling fluid out of your tissues and into your bloodstream, which your kidneys then work overtime to filter out.
Unexplained fatigue is another common early marker. When your cells can't efficiently use glucose for energy, you end up feeling tired even after adequate rest.
Slow-healing cuts or frequent infections can also signal elevated blood sugar, since high glucose levels affect circulation and your body's ability to fight infection.
Blurred vision, though often temporary, happens when fluid shifts affect the lens of the eye — it's frequently one of the first things patients notice and dismiss as eye strain.

If you're experiencing two or more of these signs, a simple blood sugar and HbA1c test can clarify where you stand. Catching prediabetes or early type 2 diabetes gives you far more room to manage it through lifestyle changes alone, before medication becomes necessary.

sections.heading: How we use it
